evidence_packet.evidence_text: A paramedic has been struck off for telling a woman suffering a stroke to stop acting "like a baby" and accused of them of lying about their pain The Healthcare Professionals Tribunal Service heard Rachel Claire Lemonofides made "inappropriate and degrading" comments heard on a 999 call at the woman's home in 2024 It found Lemonofides was guilty of racially motivated discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity and breached professional boundaries The patient underwent emergency surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester, and was diagnosed with a brain bleed and abdominal aortic aneurysm. Police are investigating after the Believe Achieve CIC project in Stoneclough, Bolton, was targeted on Monday night. The bike hub was being built after reports of young people in the area using illegal motorised bikes - and the group aims to give youngsters access to bicycles while teaching road safety and maintenance skills. Tunde Olasupo, project founder, says the site was "stormed" by people who vandalised a surrounding fence and forcibly opened a container that will house the hub. They added there had been opposition to the project, with concerns about further antisocial behaviour. There were also concerns about its location and environmental impact, Olasupo said. 'Upset' "Of course, I'm upset, and when you see something that you've worked hard for deliberately damaged, you're human, it hurts," he told BBC Radio Manchester. He said the site had been targeted before. "The objective is to balance access and community benefit with protecting and enhancing the natural environment, and that's one of the things that we're trying to make very clear to people." Image source, Believe Achieve CIC Image caption, Tunde Olasupo thanked residents who had shown the project support Believe Achieve CIC was set up in memory of Olasupo's son, Kingsley, who died in 2019, with the aim of giving young people opportunities he never got to experience. Counter terrorism police said Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, 49, of St James Road, Higher Broughton, Salford, had been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. Hakim has been remanded into custody to appear before Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday. There have so far been eight arrests in connection with the attack, however this is the first charge that "relates directly" to the morning of 2 October, when two men died as the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue was attacked by Jihad Al-Shamie. He was shot by police and died at the scene. Worshippers Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed. Assistant Chief Constable Rob Potts, from Counter Terrorism Policing North West (CTPNW) , said: "This is a significant development in our investigation, and my thoughts are with all those affected by the attack, particularly the bereaved loved ones and survivors. "We have updated them and continue to offer them as much support as possible. "Since the attack took place, we have been unwavering in our commitment to establishing the full picture behind the incident and identifying anybody who may have been involved in any way." In July, Mohammad Bashir, 31, who planned an attack on a military base with the Manchester synagogue attacker was jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years. title: Six men held after Salford raids target heroin and cocaine supply

evidence_packet.title: Six men held after Salford raids target heroin and cocaine supply
evidence_packet.lead: Six men are arrested after early morning raids on homes in Salford
evidence_packet.summary: Six men are arrested after early morning raids on homes in Salford
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Six men held after Salford raids target heroin and cocaine supply - BBC News Image caption, Six men were arrested in early morning raids By Richard Stead Reporting from in Salford Published 20 August 2026 Six men have been arrested in drugs raids which aimed to target the supply of heroin and crack cocaine in Salford. About 50 police officers were involved in the operation, which took place at five addresses in the Pendlebury and Clifton areas of the city at 0530 BST. Officers seized drugs which are believed to be cocaine and heroin, cash and two high-value mountain bikes, which are suspected to have been stolen. Ch Insp Lee Gridley said the raids were the "result of months of evidence gathering" by Swinton's neighbourhood teams to "take action against people who prey on the vulnerable". He added: "Hopefully this operation will disrupt the supply of Class A drugs across Salford and all we can do is ask communities to give us the information we need and we will act robustly." Image caption, Chief Inspector Lee Gridley urges people to give information to police Police rammed the front doors off their hinges before entering the houses and flats to search the properties and make arrests. Four of the addresses were on Hopwood Street, Pendlebury and the fifth was a flat on Castleway in the Clifton area. Image caption, Part of the operation was on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury Those arrested in the raids are being questioned over a range of suspected offences. They include possession of Class A drugs, possession with intent to supply, possession of an offensive weapon, burglary and failure to appear at court. title: The man who vowed to stop 'inhumane treatment of climbing boys'

evidence_packet.title: The man who vowed to stop 'inhumane treatment of climbing boys'
evidence_packet.lead: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
evidence_packet.summary: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

title: Godmother of rock and roll's Manchester station gig honoured

evidence_packet.title: Godmother of rock and roll's Manchester station gig honoured
evidence_packet.lead: The blues guitarist and vocalist Sister Rosetta Tharpe performed at an empty station for TV
evidence_packet.summary: The blues guitarist and vocalist Sister Rosetta Tharpe performed at an empty station for TV
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

title: North West NHS trust accused of failing to investigate deaths

evidence_packet.title: North West NHS trust accused of failing to investigate deaths
evidence_packet.lead: One of the north-west of England's biggest healthcare trusts has responded to allegations it failed to properly investigate claims patients died or were harmed during surgery Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Ho
evidence_packet.summary: One of the north-west of England's biggest healthcare trusts has responded to allegations it failed to properly investigate claims patients died or were harmed during surgery Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Ho
evidence_packet.evidence_text: One of the north-west of England's biggest healthcare trusts has responded to allegations it failed to properly investigate claims patients died or were harmed during surgery Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 , external that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims

evidence_packet.lead: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determin

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

title: Godmother of rock and roll's Manchester station gig honoured

evidence_packet.title: Godmother of rock and roll's Manchester station gig honoured
evidence_packet.lead: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with t
evidence_packet.summary: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport man puzzled as latest bizarre bin incident caught on doorbell camera What Dave Bresnahan later found out, he said, had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporte In recent weeks, a furore of bin collections across the town and its suburbs has sent residents and councillors into a frenzy. Hundreds of bins went uncollected due to their lids being 'open' by millimetres in July, while a row ensued over the council's apparent crackdown on its Now in the latest strange happenings, resident Dave Bresnahan was left baffled by what was caught on his doorbell camera. Mr Bresnahan said it had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough The resident of Bosden Farm near Hazel Grove told the Manchester Evening News : “I had just gone down to the shops. We have had all this chaos about the bins all over Stockport . It’s been going on and on and on and everyone has got absolutely fed up “What happened was I put the bin out and I had been away for a few days. I came back that morning and I thought I would only put the black bin out because the rest weren’t full.” He added: “I went to the shop to get some milk and the blue bin was out. I thought that was a bit strange. I thought maybe the neighbour had put it out.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime I stood and watched as GMP raided four new homes at 5am - four things stayed with me "It’s easy to forget the destructive criminality that is the reason for these raids - and the people whose lives it is blighting" Comments News opinion Greta Si I always say to anyone asking about my job that there are highs, and there are lows Highs might be the satisfaction of getting a really complex story over the line; reading positive feedback; a ticket to a show or artist you’ve been dying to see (contingent on a review, of course) All those things felt very far away, standing in the driving rain at 5.30am on August 20, watching a tactical aid officer saw through someone’s front door like a hot knife through butter We were on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury with officers from GMP’s Tactical Aid Unit and the Salford Neighbourhood team, watching them execute four dawn raids on properties suspected to be linked to drug dealing and burglaries in the area, with a fifth taking place in Clifton nearb It meant setting my alarm for 4am, hastily downing a coffee and a muffin on the rain-lashed M60 and rolling into a Salford police station just before 5am

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police On the streets with the cops trying to tackle one of Manchester's biggest problems The 'game changing' technology is helping GMP cut down on anti-social behaviour and crime associated with e-bikes and e-scooters Comments News On a car park in north Manchester, a group of police officers are sat in a van huddled around a screen A bird's eye view of Harpurhey is being livestreamed directly from one of Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) drones onto the monitor. The officers have intel from a civilian about a lead they're after The drone is hovering over an address and, as soon as the video confirms their suspicions, officers on the ground are sent in and three arrests are made Moments earlier, a specially trained officer stood with his remote control in the car park, sending the drone off into the sky. evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Stockport man puzzled as latest bizarre bin incident caught on doorbell camera What Dave Bresnahan later found out, he said, had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporte In recent weeks, a furore of
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport man puzzled as latest bizarre bin incident caught on doorbell camera What Dave Bresnahan later found out, he said, had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporte In recent weeks, a furore of bin collections across the town and its suburbs has sent residents and councillors into a frenzy. Hundreds of bins went uncollected due to their lids being 'open' by millimetres in July, while a row ensued over the council's apparent crackdown on its Now in the latest strange happenings, resident Dave Bresnahan was left baffled by what was caught on his doorbell camera. Mr Bresnahan said it had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough The resident of Bosden Farm near Hazel Grove told the Manchester Evening News : “I had just gone down to the shops. We have had all this chaos about the bins all over Stockport . It’s been going on and on and on and everyone has got absolutely fed up “What happened was I put the bin out and I had been away for a few days. I came back that morning and I thought I would only put the black bin out because the rest weren’t full.” He added: “I went to the shop to get some milk and the blue bin was out. I thought that was a bit strange. I thought maybe the neighbour had put it out.”

evidence_packet.summary: Wigan The fight to save Wigan’s greenbelt from concrete jungles may have just been won The removal of the land is a ‘huge and incredibly emotional moment’, campaigners say Comments News Hannah Richardson 18:21, 20 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Bridgewater We Wigan campaigners have achie
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The fight to save Wigan’s greenbelt from concrete jungles may have just been won The removal of the land is a ‘huge and incredibly emotional moment’, campaigners say Comments News Hannah Richardson 18:21, 20 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Bridgewater We Wigan campaigners have achieved a resounding victory after four controversial greenbelt sites were removed from the area's local plan Around five million square metres of employment space across the sites was to be allocated in the document under earlier town hall thinking. The local plan sets out Wigan council's vision for future development in the borough, including, crucially, where building projects are all Town hall bosses have now said they believe they can still meet the borough’s employment needs without building on the land at Bridgewater West, in Astley; west of Winwick Lane, in Lowton; at Aspull Common, in Leigh; and to the north Junction 26 of the M6, near Wigan. While plann Wigan council has also set out its intention to object to a fifth area of development, the Gibfield Park masterplan. The latter scheme has been allocated in the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone policy and has the potential to deliver 500 homes and 375,000sqm of sheds The various schemes have been branded an ‘abomination’, a ‘concrete jungle’ and an ‘obliteration of nature’ by residents demanding developers leave their greenspaces alone

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime I stood and watched as GMP raided four new homes at 5am - four things stayed with me "It’s easy to forget the destructive criminality that is the reason for these raids - and the people whose lives it is blighting" Comments News opinion Greta Si I always say to anyone asking about my job that there are highs, and there are lows Highs might be the satisfaction of getting a really complex story over the line; reading positive feedback; a ticket to a show or artist you’ve been dying to see (contingent on a review, of course) All those things felt very far away, standing in the driving rain at 5.30am on August 20, watching a tactical aid officer saw through someone’s front door like a hot knife through butter We were on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury with officers from GMP’s Tactical Aid Unit and the Salford Neighbourhood team, watching them execute four dawn raids on properties suspected to be linked to drug dealing and burglaries in the area, with a fifth taking place in Clifton nearb It meant setting my alarm for 4am, hastily downing a coffee and a muffin on the rain-lashed M60 and rolling into a Salford police station just before 5am

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheadle and Cheadle Hulme School opens doors for milestone event for children's charity Rainbow Trust The charity supports the families of children with life-threatenng and terminal illnesses, but doesn't receive any central government funding. News D A Greater Manchester school played host to a special celebration for a charity that has been helping families who have a child with life-threatening or terminal illnesses for the past 40 years. The Rainbow Trust, a children's care charity, hosted a special family fun day at Brads The charity has been established nationally for 40 years, and for 22 years has had its own Manchester Care team supporting local families. Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come together and enjoy some much needed family fun during the school holidays. Children played alongside their siblings and families, and got to enjoy face painting, a treasure hunt, games, arts and cr Among those at the event were Evie and her family, who have been helped by the Rainbow Trust. Evie’s mum Vicky said: "As parents we are caring for Evie 24/7 and having support from Rainbow Trust brings Evie so much joy. Evie was born at 29 weeks and has been very poorly having ha "Without Rainbow Trust and Family Support Worker Emma’s support, life would be a lot more difficult."

evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale Partner of man, 31, found dead in Rochdale says 'I want him to be remembered as he was' as murder probe dropped Nathan Haigh died at a flat on Great Howarth on August 11 News Paul Britton Reporter and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news repo The partner of a man who was
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Partner of man, 31, found dead in Rochdale says 'I want him to be remembered as he was' as murder probe dropped Nathan Haigh died at a flat on Great Howarth on August 11 News Paul Britton Reporter and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news repo The partner of a man who was found dead at a flat in Rochdale has described him as being 'like the sunshine' in a tribute for him Nathan Haigh, 31, was found unresponsive by emergency services at a flat on Great Howarth, near Wardle, just before 7.40pm last Tuesday (August 11). Police were initially called to the scene over reports of an 'unexpected death' Following Mr Haigh's death, a 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder . Detectives said they were exploring 'several lines of enquiries in what initially appeared to be suspicious circumstances' In an update issued on August 19, a Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said that 'following extensive enquiries, detectives have ruled out murder as a line of enquiry.' The woman arrested for murder was released and remains on bail for assault Rebecca Hamer, 36, has now shared a tribute for Mr Haigh. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire International DJ turned EncroChat drug trafficker absconds from prison Officers are trying to trace Kyle Chase News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 15:53, 20 Aug 2026 Updated 15:54, 20 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Kyle Chase (Image: Merseyside Police) An international DJ who was unmasked as an EncroChat drug trafficker has absconded from prison, police have said Police in Cheshire have issued an appeal for information over the whereabouts of Kyle Chase, who they said was last seen leaving HMP Thorn Cross in Warrington last Friday (August 14) The now 41-year-old was jailed for 12 years in 2024, at Liverpool Crown Court, which heard he was a 'highly trusted conspirator with extensive involvement in the drug world.' Also known as Kyle Muldoon, he had previously carved out a reputation in the international dance music scene under his DJ name Eldon - a reference to the Eldonian Village where he lived He played shows at festivals and events in the likes of Croatia and Ecuador and opened Spray Shop - a former garage transformed into a dance music nightclub close to Bramley Moore docks in Liverpool - in February 2023

evidence_packet.evidence_text: GCSE results Greater Manchester pupils celebrate GCSE results as one borough shines brightest and schools secure record-breaking year GCSE pupils received their grades this morning Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer , Bethan Finigh It was an emotional day across Greater Manchester as thousands of students finally discovered their GCSE results, with nervous faces turning to smiles, tears and celebrations as they opened their long-awaited envelopes on Thursday (August 20) morning The day they had been waiting for comes just a week after a successful A Level Results Day , when students across the region celebrated a string of momentous successes Here at the Manchester Evening News , we travelled across Greater Manchester to meet some of the hardworking students behind the results, capturing the nerves, excitement and sheer relief as they ripped open their brown envelopes and discovered their futures The day painted a mixed picture across Greater Manchester. Trafford became the only area ranked in England's top 20 that is outside the south with a huge 39.7% of grades received by pupils in the borough of 7 or above Meanwhile, Rochdale was one of the worst performing councils with 13.2% at a grade 7 or above. Elsewhere across Greater Manchester, Salford was at 18.1%, Stockport 24.8%, Oldham 16.7%, Bolton 20.1% and Manchester 22.5%

evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police On the streets with the cops trying to tackle one of Manchester's biggest problems The 'game changing' technology is helping GMP cut down on anti-social behaviour and crime associated with e-bikes and e-scooters Comments News On a car park in north Manch
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police On the streets with the cops trying to tackle one of Manchester's biggest problems The 'game changing' technology is helping GMP cut down on anti-social behaviour and crime associated with e-bikes and e-scooters Comments News On a car park in north Manchester, a group of police officers are sat in a van huddled around a screen A bird's eye view of Harpurhey is being livestreamed directly from one of Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) drones onto the monitor. The officers have intel from a civilian about a lead they're after The drone is hovering over an address and, as soon as the video confirms their suspicions, officers on the ground are sent in and three arrests are made Moments earlier, a specially trained officer stood with his remote control in the car park, sending the drone off into the sky. Now, three men are sat in the back of a police van after GMP seized a stolen bike and subsequently found a machete in the house View 4 Images The drones are also used at events like concerts or football matches (Image: Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport man puzzled as latest bizarre bin incident caught on doorbell camera What Dave Bresnahan later found out, he said, had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporte In recent weeks, a furore of bin collections across the town and its suburbs has sent residents and councillors into a frenzy. Hundreds of bins went uncollected due to their lids being 'open' by millimetres in July, while a row ensued over the council's apparent crackdown on its Now in the latest strange happenings, resident Dave Bresnahan was left baffled by what was caught on his doorbell camera. Mr Bresnahan said it had never happened before in his 25 years living on the borough The resident of Bosden Farm near Hazel Grove told the Manchester Evening News : “I had just gone down to the shops. We have had all this chaos about the bins all over Stockport . It’s been going on and on and on and everyone has got absolutely fed up “What happened was I put the bin out and I had been away for a few days. I came back that morning and I thought I would only put the black bin out because the rest weren’t full.” He added: “I went to the shop to get some milk and the blue bin was out. I thought that was a bit strange. I thought maybe the neighbour had put it out.”

evidence_packet.summary: Wigan The fight to save Wigan’s greenbelt from concrete jungles may have just been won The removal of the land is a ‘huge and incredibly emotional moment’, campaigners say Comments News Hannah Richardson 18:21, 20 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Bridgewater We Wigan campaigners have achie
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The fight to save Wigan’s greenbelt from concrete jungles may have just been won The removal of the land is a ‘huge and incredibly emotional moment’, campaigners say Comments News Hannah Richardson 18:21, 20 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Bridgewater We Wigan campaigners have achieved a resounding victory after four controversial greenbelt sites were removed from the area's local plan Around five million square metres of employment space across the sites was to be allocated in the document under earlier town hall thinking. The local plan sets out Wigan council's vision for future development in the borough, including, crucially, where building projects are all Town hall bosses have now said they believe they can still meet the borough’s employment needs without building on the land at Bridgewater West, in Astley; west of Winwick Lane, in Lowton; at Aspull Common, in Leigh; and to the north Junction 26 of the M6, near Wigan. While plann Wigan council has also set out its intention to object to a fifth area of development, the Gibfield Park masterplan. The latter scheme has been allocated in the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone policy and has the potential to deliver 500 homes and 375,000sqm of sheds The various schemes have been branded an ‘abomination’, a ‘concrete jungle’ and an ‘obliteration of nature’ by residents demanding developers leave their greenspaces alone

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime I stood and watched as GMP raided four new homes at 5am - four things stayed with me "It’s easy to forget the destructive criminality that is the reason for these raids - and the people whose lives it is blighting" Comments News opinion Greta Si I always say to anyone asking about my job that there are highs, and there are lows Highs might be the satisfaction of getting a really complex story over the line; reading positive feedback; a ticket to a show or artist you’ve been dying to see (contingent on a review, of course) All those things felt very far away, standing in the driving rain at 5.30am on August 20, watching a tactical aid officer saw through someone’s front door like a hot knife through butter We were on Hopwood Street in Pendlebury with officers from GMP’s Tactical Aid Unit and the Salford Neighbourhood team, watching them execute four dawn raids on properties suspected to be linked to drug dealing and burglaries in the area, with a fifth taking place in Clifton nearb It meant setting my alarm for 4am, hastily downing a coffee and a muffin on the rain-lashed M60 and rolling into a Salford police station just before 5am

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheadle and Cheadle Hulme School opens doors for milestone event for children's charity Rainbow Trust The charity supports the families of children with life-threatenng and terminal illnesses, but doesn't receive any central government funding. News D A Greater Manchester school played host to a special celebration for a charity that has been helping families who have a child with life-threatening or terminal illnesses for the past 40 years. The Rainbow Trust, a children's care charity, hosted a special family fun day at Brads The charity has been established nationally for 40 years, and for 22 years has had its own Manchester Care team supporting local families. Joining the celebration was inspirational fundraiser Dr Michael Josephson MBE , who has raised £500,000 for the Rainbow Trust at his charity The event was an opportunity for those families supported by Rainbow Trust to come together and enjoy some much needed family fun during the school holidays. Children played alongside their siblings and families, and got to enjoy face painting, a treasure hunt, games, arts and cr Among those at the event were Evie and her family, who have been helped by the Rainbow Trust. Evie’s mum Vicky said: "As parents we are caring for Evie 24/7 and having support from Rainbow Trust brings Evie so much joy. Evie was born at 29 weeks and has been very poorly having ha "Without Rainbow Trust and Family Support Worker Emma’s support, life would be a lot more difficult."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: GCSE results LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 18 hours ago GCSE Results Day 2026 RECAP as schools reach record-breaking grades Results and reaction from schools across the region as students find out their GCSE grades GCSE exam results at The Barlow RC High, On Thursday (August 20), 15 and 16-year-olds who sat their exams in May and June discovered whether they got the grades they needed for A levels, T levels, BTECs or apprenticeships Across the UK, the proportion of GCSE entries awarded top grades has risen from last year but the rate scoring a decent pass has returned to pre-pandemic levels. In north-west England, 18.9% of entries received grade 7 or above, up slightly from 18.8% in 2025 The results were made available to schools on Wednesday (August 19) and have been available to collect from schools from 8am. Schools across Greater Manchester have issued their own guidance on how and when students can collect results The grading system for GCSE results were revamped back in 2017 and now use a numbered system, replacing the traditional A* to G letter results. According to Ofqual, a grade 7 is comparable the old grade A; a grade 4 to the old C grade and the new grade 1 to the old grade G. Here Employers, universities and others who previously set entry requirements of at least a grade C, would now be at least a grade 4. Students who receive a grade 3 or below in GCSE maths or English language will generally have to continue studying the subject

Trafford became the only area ranked in England's top 20 that is outside the south with a huge 39.7% of grades received by pupils in the borough of 7 or above Meanwhile, Rochdale was one of the worst performing councils with 13.2% at a grade 7 or above. evidence_packet.summary: Hundreds of NHS operating theatre staff at four hospitals in Greater Manchester will be back on strike for three days next week in a dispute about overtime payments More than 350 Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA) employees, including nurses, clinical support workers a
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hundreds of NHS operating theatre staff at four hospitals in Greater Manchester will be back on strike for three days next week in a dispute about overtime payments More than 350 Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA) employees, including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers, at Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield Hospital in Bury, are walking out on Monday 24, Wednesday 26 and UNISON says an offer to resolve the dispute was initially tabled by NCA bosses but withdrawn before discussions could take place The row centres on the trust’s use of an outside agency – NHS Professionals (NHSP) – to manage overtime When covering staff shortages, staff are entitled to time-and-a-half pay. However, in some cases staff earn less than they would on a normal shift, with some missing out on more than £80 per shift, adds the union Operating theatre staff were previously on picket lines at all four sites in June

Plus there’s the celebs backing the re-funding of Jodrell Bank obs The sun rose this morning on Bev Craig’s Greater Manchester. Already dubbed the “Queen of the North”, the unassuming, low-ego former council leader is a departure from her predecessor Andy Burnham, though in terms of policy she is expected to continue on the same path he has set Rumours now circulate about who will be running her office. evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

title: 300 more school places for Altrincham secured as council buys Loreto Prep site

evidence_packet.title: 300 more school places for Altrincham secured as council buys Loreto Prep site
evidence_packet.lead: The first additional places are expected from September 2027
evidence_packet.summary: The first additional places are expected from September 2027
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The first additional places are expected from September 2027 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has completed the purchase of the former Loreto Preparatory School site on Dunham Road - ending years of uncertainty over the three-acre plot and securing it for the expansion of neighbouring North Cestrian School The acquisition, funded by a Department for Education capital grant, will allow North Cestrian to add up to 300 secondary school places A feasibility study is now underway, with the first additional places expected from September 2027 and the full expansion complete by September 2028 The deal was struck by Trafford's Development and Education teams working alongside Hamblin Education Trust, which runs North Cestrian It draws a line under a two-year campaign that began when Loreto Prep - an independent Catholic primary school with a 114-year history - unexpectedly closed in July 2023 , citing declining pupil numbers and financial pressures

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter terrorism police said Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, 49, of St James Road, Higher Broughton, Salford, had been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity Hakim has been remanded into custody to appear before Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday There have so far been eight arrests in connection with the attack, however this is the first charge that "relates directly" to the morning of 2 October, when two men died as the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue was attacked by Jihad Al-Shamie. evidence_packet.title: North West NHS trust accused of failing to investigate deaths
evidence_packet.lead: Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 that the
evidence_packet.summary: Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 that the
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims Other allegations raised in the report include staff suggesting their accounts of serious harm or death are "shut down or not investigated properly"

evidence_packet.summary: Kevin Lewis, also known as Abdul Kareem, died in hospital two days after police were called to a disturbance at an address in Blackley, Manchester, at about 02:45 BST on Saturday The 36-year-old was described by his family as "a devout Muslim" and "a kind and caring person whose
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Kevin Lewis, also known as Abdul Kareem, died in hospital two days after police were called to a disturbance at an address in Blackley, Manchester, at about 02:45 BST on Saturday The 36-year-old was described by his family as "a devout Muslim" and "a kind and caring person whose warmth touched the hearts of everyone who knew him" A woman, 29, initially arrested on suspicion of wounding and assaulting a police officer in connection with the incident has now been arrested on suspicion of murder. She has been bailed pending further investigation Lewis's family said he was "a loving father, son, brother, uncle and dear friend" "He was a kind and caring person whose warmth touched the hearts of everyone who knew him," they said They said his four "beautiful daughters" aged eight months, three, six and nine, "were his pride and joy, and his love for them was beyond words"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Zherko Rasul Osman, 24, suffered serious stab wounds on Chapel Street in the Levenshulme area of Manchester just after 19:00 BST on Saturday and died at the scene, Greater Manchester Police said A 23-year-old man, who was arrested on suspicion of murder on Tuesday, remains in custody In a tribute, Osman's brother described him as "a kind, friendly and loving person who never looked for trouble or wanted to harm anyone" "He was loved and respected by his friends, his mates and the neighbours in the community where he lived," he said "He had a good heart and would always be remembered for the warmth and happiness he brought to those around him "His life was taken so suddenly and for no reason, leaving a pain and emptiness that words cannot describe."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.lead: Друзья, а вы давно ощущали настоящую магию театра?
evidence_packet.summary: Друзья, а вы давно ощущали настоящую магию театра? 29 ноября 2026 года в Logan Hall — легендарная «Скамейка» с Алексеем Паниным
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Спектакль «Скамейка» в Лондоне | Алексей Панин | 29 ноября 2026 :: EventFirst Home double_arrow Events double_arrow Спектакль "Скамейка" On sale Спектакль "Скамейка" schedule 29 Nov 2026 Sunday, 19:00 location_on Logan Hall 20 Bedford Way, London WC1H 0AL balcony 18:00 gpp_maybe NO REFUNDS Buy On MAP Buy Tickets Logan Hall £30.00 Select Logan Hall £35.00 Sold Out Logan Hall £40.00 Select Logan Hall £45.00 Select Logan Hall £50.00 Select Logan Hall £55.00 Select Logan Hall £60.00 Select Logan Hall £65.00 Sold Out Logan Hall £70.00 Select Logan Hall £80.00 Select Logan Hall £85.00 Sold Out Logan Hall £90.00 Sold Out Logan Hall £95.00 Select Друзья, а вы давно ощущали настоящую магию театра? 29 ноября 2026 года в Logan Hall — легендарная «Скамейка» с Алексеем Паниным. После аншлагов в Европе и США спектакль впервые приезжает в Лондон. 📍 University College London, Level 1, 20 Bedford Way, London WC1H 0AL 🕕 DOORS: 18:00 🕖 SHOW: 19:00 «Скамейка» — знаменитая пьеса, когда-то блистательно сыгранная Олегом Ефремовым и Татьяной Дорониной на сцене МХАТа, а затем покорившая театральные площадки по всему миру. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Campaign for Business Campaign for Business Campaign for Business is the Chamber’s blueprint for business growth in Greater Manchester. Since his arrival in England, Fernandes has rarely been shy about making his feelings known on the pitch This could be by either confronting a referee, throwing his arms in the air or remonstrating over a decision he feels has gone against him. Recognising this, Scott tried to disarm the Portugal midfielder with humour before refereeing him for the first time in 2022 "It was straight after the Qatar World Cup," Scott explained on the Under The Cosh podcast . "We always have this thing where we're waiting in the tunnel Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость.
